scope: Observed command descriptions, not per-command business acceptance

action.batch.label: Batch…
action.batch.params: {commands: [{command, params}] (the action's steps), source?: folder (default) | datasets, folder? (required for folder: the source folder), includeSubdirs?: false, destination?: none (default: leave each file open) | saveAndClose (save over the source and close) | folder (save or export into destinationFolder and close), destinationFolder? (required when destination is folder; also the folder Override Save/Export write into), overrideOpen?: true (skip document.open / file.open steps: the batch opens each source file), overrideSave?: true (point document.save / file.save / file.saveAs at destinationFolder/{stem}.{ext}), overrideExport?: true (point document.export / document.exportForScreens / document.exportSelection the same way), stopOnError?: true, label?} play the commands on every readable file in folder (and its subfolders when includeSubdirs), or on every data set of the open document (source: datasets; File + Data Set Name for Override Save/Export). Caps: 500 files or data sets, 8 folder levels, 256 steps. Batches cannot nest. → {processed: [{path|dataset, result|error}…], count, failed, stopped}

dataset.export.label: Export Data Sets…
dataset.export.params: {path?} write every dataset as CSV (header: name, then variables); without path → {csv, datasets}

dataset.import.label: Import Data Sets…
dataset.import.params: {path? | data? | dataBase64? | csv?} load datasets from CSV (header: name, then variable names; one row per dataset). Rows whose name already exists are replaced → {imported, updated, names}

dimension.applyToAll.label: Apply to All
dimension.applyToAll.params: {id?: dimension id (default the first selected dimension)} gives every dimension in the document that dimension's style (its scale too), as one undo step → {ids}

dimension.create.label: Create Dimension
dimension.create.params: {mode?: linear|angular|radius|diameter, a?: [x,y], b?: [x,y], vertex?: [x,y], source?: {kind: segment, edge: {node,subpath,segment}}|{kind: angle, first: edge, second: edge}|{kind: circle, node}|{kind: arc, edge}|{kind: points, a?, b?, vertex?: {node,subpath,anchor}}, offset?: pt, options?: {units: in|mm|pt|pc|px|cm|m|ft|yd, precision: 0-6, scale: drawing:real, hideUnits, lineWeight, lineType: solid|dashed|dotted, lineColor: [r,g,b], arrowStyle: filled|open|tick|none, arrowScale: %, extensionWeight, extensionType, extensionColor, extensionOffset, extensionLength, hideExtensions, fontFamily, fontStyle, fontSize, textColor, textPosition: away|between, textAlignment: left|center|right, textOffset}} → {id,label}; linked measurements follow source edits

dimension.update.label: Update Dimensions
dimension.update.params: {ids?: [dimension ids] (default selection), options?: dimension options, offset?: pt} restyle or move existing dimensions → {ids}

document.exportPresets.delete.label: Delete Export Preset
document.exportPresets.delete.params: {name} delete a saved batch export preset (built-in ones stay) → {deleted}

document.exportPresets.list.label: Export Presets
document.exportPresets.list.params: {} → {presets: [{name, builtIn, settings}]} the built-in batch export presets (Logo Package, Print-Ready PDF), then the saved ones; any name works as document.exportForScreens' exportPreset

document.exportPresets.save.label: Save Export Preset
document.exportPresets.save.params: {name, settings: {formats, settings, preset, name, prefix, counterStart, counterPer, folders, subfolders, includeBleed, antiAlias, folder, fullDocument} (as document.exportForScreens; other keys are left out)} save (or replace) a batch export preset, kept with the preferences; built-in names are refused → {name, created, settings}

object.intertwine.arrange.label: Arrange Intertwine Area
object.intertwine.arrange.params: {id?: Intertwine group (default: the selected one), at?: [x,y] (the overlap area under this point, as a click picks it) | area?: [[x,y]…] (a closed polygon drawn around overlap areas: every area whose inside it encloses), order?: toggle|front|back (toggle: the object drawn right below the top comes to the front, so two objects swap), member?: id (front and back: the object to move; default: front brings the object right below the top, back sends the top one)} → {count: areas changed, top: [id of the object now on top in each area]}

object.intertwine.edit.label: Edit
object.intertwine.edit.params: {} choose the Intertwine tool for the selected Intertwine group (Esc or Enter goes back to the tool before)

object.intertwine.make.label: Make
object.intertwine.make.params: {ids?: two or more objects (default: the selection)} put the objects in an Intertwine group and choose the Intertwine tool, which arranges its overlap areas (object.intertwine.arrange) → {id}

object.intertwine.release.label: Release
object.intertwine.release.params: {} give the objects of the selected Intertwine groups back as they were made, dropping the arranged areas → {ids}

select.update.label: Update Selection
select.update.params: {} make the saved selection last recalled (`select.recall`) hold the selected objects instead of its own, in one undo step → {name}

symbol.options.label: Symbol Options…
symbol.options.params: {name?, newName?, registration?: 0..8, exportType?: movieClip|graphic} rename a symbol and/or set Symbol Options › Registration and Export Type (default name: current) → {name, registration, exportType}

type.resetHorizontalScale.label: Reset Horizontal Scale
type.resetHorizontalScale.params: {ids?: [id…]} set the horizontal scale to 100% (as the Character panel shows it, the object's own transform included) in all the text of the type objects in `ids`, else in the text the Type tool has selected (nothing at a caret), else in every selected type object, as one undo step → {ids}

type.resetTracking.label: Reset Tracking and Kerning
type.resetTracking.params: {ids?: [id…]} set tracking to 0 and kerning to Auto (the font's own kerning, which the Character panel shows as 0) in all the text of the type objects in `ids`, else in the text the Type tool has selected (at a caret: only the kerning of the character before it), else in every selected type object, as one undo step → {ids}

type.size.decreaseByFive.label: Decrease Font Size by Five Steps
type.size.decreaseByFive.params: {} type.step {attribute: size, by: -5}: five times the Size/Leading increment (typeSizeIncrement)

type.size.increaseByFive.label: Increase Font Size by Five Steps
type.size.increaseByFive.params: {} type.step {attribute: size, by: 5}: five times the Size/Leading increment (typeSizeIncrement)

variable.makeGraphDynamic.label: Make Graph Dynamic
variable.makeGraphDynamic.params: {} define a graph variable over the selected graph root(s), named after it and bound to it; each dataset row supplies CSV as graph.setData

variable.makeImageDynamic.label: Make Image Dynamic
variable.makeImageDynamic.params: {} define an image variable over the selection, named after it and bound to it

artboard.fitToArt.old: {index?} the artboard fits the art that shows (with its strokes and effects; hidden objects and layers, guides and template layers don't count)
artboard.fitToArt.current: {index?: n | indices?: [n…] (0-based; the app passes the selected artboards: the Artboard tool's, else the active one; default: the first)} each artboard fits the art on it that shows (with its strokes and effects; hidden objects and layers, guides and template layers don't count), in one undo step: an object counts for every artboard its bounds overlap, and a group or clipping layer counts as one object; an artboard with no art stays as it is, and the command fails when no artboard it names has art

artboard.fitToSelection.current: {index?: n (0-based; the app passes the active artboard; default: the first)} the artboard fits the selected art (with its strokes)

assets.add.old: {ids?: [id…] (default: the selected objects), multiple?: true (an asset per object; false: one asset of them all), name?: (the asset's name, when it makes one)} collect art as assets for Window › Asset Export and Export for Screens' Assets tab, named after the object (else Asset 1, Asset 2…); art already collected as such an asset keeps it → {assets: [asset id…] (in order), added: n}. Assets follow their art: moving it moves the crop, deleting it removes it from the asset
assets.add.current: {ids?: [id…] (default: the selected objects; a layer id collects the art under it, including in its sublayers), multiple?: true (an asset per object; false: one asset of them all), name?: (the asset's name, when it makes one)} collect art as assets for Window › Asset Export and Export for Screens' Assets tab, named after the object (else Asset 1, Asset 2…); art already collected as such an asset keeps it → {assets: [asset id…] (in order), added: n}. Assets follow their art: moving it moves the crop, deleting it removes it from the asset
